title: The Edge of the Green
story:
James was a monkey who paid close attention. He knew the precise give of a fig before it fell. He knew the hollow whistle the north wind made through dry bamboo. He knew the exact afternoon minute when the cicadas would grow tired of their own buzzing. But he did not know what lay past the last ironwood tree, because no one in the high branches ever wandered far enough to ask.

Today, the green stopped. It did not fade gently into thinner brush; it simply broke open against the sky. Before him lay a vast descent of rolling golden hills, yawning under an enormous dome of pale blue air. When James felt the familiar flutter in his ribs that signaled he was both nervous and deeply curious, he performed his ritual: he closed his eyes and counted three distinct sounds. One: the papery rustle of a cicada wing. Two: the creak of the canopy boughs swaying behind him. Three: a distant, rushing breath of wind that smelled of sun-warmed rock and unfamiliar soil.

Satisfied that the world was in working order, James stepped down from the bough and planted his bare feet into the warm red dirt. It was shockingly firm after a lifetime of yielding moss and springy bark. He paused, touched two fingers to his chest, and gave the vast openness a polite nod. "Pleased to meet you, whatever comes next," he murmured to the breeze. It was the only proper way to greet an unknown place.

He did not run, and he did not turn back toward the safety of the shade. Instead, he walked until the jungle’s heavy shadow slipped away from his shoulders, finally climbing onto a flat granite boulder that held the day's heat. Far out across the golden plains, where the haze of distance blurred the ridge lines, a thin, crooked thread of pale grey smoke rose into the air, rising straight and patient before unraveling into nothing. James rested his chin on his knees and watched it climb.
location: a sun-warmed granite boulder on the hillside just beyond the jungle edge
